subject: Vaulted rack egress and service choreography — control/data orchestration review
messages:
From: Anna Lopez <anna@tilbury.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Vaulted rack egress & service choreography — initial diagram and ask

Jonas / Marissa / Kim,

Thanks for jumping on this quickly. Attached is our first-pass vaulted-rack diagram for the private deploy in our primary colo. The key ask: ensure control-plane management (Redwood control plane agents) can reach the management endpoints without opening broad egress and that data-plane inference traffic stays on our tenant fabric with a strict egress policy to upstream telemetry and KMS.

High-level constraints from our side:
- Vaulted racks are behind an on-site perimeter NAT for outbound to the internet (shared public IP pool).
- All KMS/HSM traffic must go over a dedicated peered interface to our key vault cluster (no hairpin).
- We require mTLS to the control-plane, and BGP fronting for inter-colo failover.

Attachments: vaulted_rack_diagram_v2.pdf (diagram).

Can you review and call out where we should place proxies/sidecars, whether we need an egress relay (NAT gateway vs. dedicated edge proxy), and how control-plane heartbeats should be routed to avoid telemetry leakage?

-- Anna
Anna Lopez
Head of Infrastructure, Tilbury Financial
[attachment: vaulted_rack_diagram_v2.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna@tilbury.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Vaulted rack egress & service choreography — initial diagram and ask

Anna — thanks for the diagram, looks clear. Quick read / high-level recommendations before we dive into the wiring: 

1) Control-plane reachability
- We recommend a narrow outbound allowlist from the management VLAN to a small set of Redwood control-plane endpoints (FQDNs + IPs). For vaulted racks where you only have shared NAT, use an edge proxy (dedicated outbound egress proxy) so we can terminate TLS from the host to the proxy and then to Redwood; that preserves cert pinning and avoids exposing host IPs.
- Heartbeats: use a short UDP/TCP keepalive to a control-plane VIP with retry/backoff. If you need stronger isolation, we can peer a management VPC via a filtered peering session limited to TCP/443 and our control-plane ASN.

2) Data-plane and inference traffic
- Keep inference traffic local to the tenant fabric. Our serving runtime can run in the vaulted rack and use local KV cache and batching. For telemetry/metrics, push via an internal telemetry relay (sidecar) that only egresses to your telemetry collectors — not to upstream Redwood.

3) KMS/HSM and key operations
- Don't route KMS traffic through the shared NAT. Use a dedicated peered interface (L3) from the rack to your key vault cluster; use mTLS mutual auth and network ACLs. If you need an HSM-backed signer inside the rack, we can run a small signing proxy that holds only ephemeral credentials.

4) Egress options (pros/cons)
- NAT gateway (simple) — minimal infra but loses host-level identity; needs IP allowlist at Redwood side.
- Dedicated edge proxy (recommended) — preserves identity, allows header-based routing and per-tenant backoff. Slightly more ops but better for canary/fallback.

Next step: Marissa / Kim can you sketch a short runbook for cutover (controls, cert rotation schedule, rollback)? I can compile and include a canary plan (10% traffic, pinned model variant, fallback to hosted model) and a short acceptance checklist.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: proposed_egress_options.md (text/markdown)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Anna Lopez <anna@tilbury.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Vaulted rack egress & service choreography — runbook notes

Looping in a couple of operational constraints and cert guidance: 

- Cert rotation: we'll use short-lived leaf certs (7 days) issued by Tilbury's internal CA and accept them at the Redwood side for the private control-plane. We need a cert distribution plan for the clusters inside the vaulted rack (systemd timer or init container for on-host workloads).
- HSM connections: confirm port and IP ranges for the HSM cluster. If the HSM enforces client IP allowlists, we need a stable egress IP (edge proxy recommended).
- Observability: telemetry must be forwarded to your internal collector. Redwood can ship metrics as a push to an internal endpoint; avoid plaintext telemetry to public endpoints.

Action items for cutover runbook (first draft):
- Pre-cutover: confirm peering or proxy IPs, validate cert chain, baseline latency/seq-loss.
- Canary: deploy runtime in 1 vault, route 10% inference traffic, verify KV cache hit-rate and latency SLOs.
- Cutover: increase traffic in 3 steps (10 / 40 / 100) with rollback triggers on error rate or token-cost spikes.
- Post-cutover: 24h monitoring window and a 7-day cert rotation verification.

I attached a short checklist and added comments on the vaulted_rack_diagram where we suggest the proxy placement.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: operational-cutover-checklist.md (text/markdown)]
